title: Samsung Refrigerator 5E / SE Error Code: Ice Maker Fix
metaDescription: Samsung fridge showing 5E or SE and the ice maker stopped working? Here's what the code means and how to fix a frozen or jammed ice maker yourself.
symptom: The display shows "5E" or "SE", the ice maker stops making ice, and the auger may make a grinding or clicking sound.
toolsNeeded: Hair dryer (low heat) or warm towels
partsNeeded: Replacement ice maker assembly (only if it doesn't recover after a full thaw)

steps.heading: Understand what the code means
steps.body: 5E (or SE, depending on model/firmware) means the ice maker's auger motor is drawing too much current — almost always because ice has jammed or fused solid around the auger, not because the motor itself is broken.

steps.heading: Power down the ice maker
steps.body: From the fridge's control panel, turn off Ice Maker mode (or use the off-switch, usually on the side of the unit in the freezer). This stops the auger from repeatedly trying and re-triggering the fault.

steps.heading: Remove and empty the ice bucket
steps.body: Take out the ice bucket/bin and empty it completely. Check the auger and the chute for a solid clump of fused ice — this is the most common cause of 5E/SE.

steps.heading: Thaw the ice maker assembly itself
steps.body: With the bucket out, use a hair dryer on low heat (held several inches away) or a warm, damp towel to melt any ice built up around the auger motor housing and the dispenser chute. A full thaw can take 2-4 hours if you leave the freezer door propped and skip the hair dryer.

steps.heading: Dry everything and power back on
steps.body: Once fully thawed, dry the bin and chute thoroughly (residual water will just refreeze), reinstall the bucket, and turn Ice Maker mode back on. Give it a few hours to resume normal cycles.

whenToCallAPro: If the code returns immediately after a full thaw and dry-out with no ice jam present, the auger motor or control board itself has likely failed and needs professional diagnosis — this isn't a jam you can clear by thawing again.
safetyWarnings: Unplug the refrigerator (or switch off Ice Maker mode) before reaching into the ice maker assembly to avoid the auger motor engaging on your fingers.
Never use a hair dryer on high heat directly against plastic ice maker components — it can warp or crack them.
Don't use a knife or hard tool to chip out fused ice — you can puncture the evaporator coil behind the ice maker, which is an expensive repair.
